The paradox of infinite language creates a sense of futility in the search for meaning, as the sheer volume of possibilities leads to meaninglessness. Finally, the library's impact on reality and knowledge suggests that knowledge is always provisional, and that truth is always relative. As the author notes, "The universe (which others call the Library) is composed of an indefinite, perhaps infinite number of hexagonal galleries… Though I am ignorant of the meaning of the phrase, I repeat that the Library is unlimited."
